transliteration: sarveṣām ardhino mukhyās tad ardhenādhino 'pare / tṛtīyinas tṛtīyāṃśāś caturthāṃśāś ca pādinaḥ //
sph_interpretive_translation: All beings possess inherent capacity; some are principal holders of half, others hold authority through a derivative quarter, tertiary beings govern a third part, and those of the fourth order manage a fourth portion.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority is hierarchically distributed based on inherent capacity
Causation arises from conscious participation in dharma
Restoration occurs through alignment with one's capacity tier
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that judicial authority must be proportionally assigned according to the conscious capacity of the presiding body. Responsibility is neither arbitrary nor punitive but calibrated to the integrity and realization level of the judge or panel.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals capacity as the causal basis for lawful action. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows sequential unfolding of roles without moral judgment. Proportional responsibility aligns with svabhāva-determined function. The non-punitive reality rule confirms no suffering arises—only realignment of function.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Reassign duties based on evolved consciousness levels
Initiate completion processes for unfulfilled responsibilities
Facilitate integration of lower-tier actors into higher-capacity functions
Restore systemic balance by recalibrating role-based authority
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source-Authority. Dharma is restored through capacity-conscious alignment. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness alone is the ultimate adjudicator.
